summary.headline: RIR Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.3% YoY to Rs 27.16 crore, EBITDA Rs 3.98 crore, with Odisha epi-wafer output targeted from Q3 FY27.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 27.16 crore (up 29.3% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 3.98 crore and EPS of 39 paisa. Margin improvement was attributed to passing on raw-material (copper, gold, silver) cost increases to customers, with about 80-85% pass-through, plus procurement and vendor negotiation gains. The Odisha epitaxy facility is nearing commissioning: power connection is nearly done, and epi operations are expected by end-Q2 FY27, with epi-wafer revenue from Q3. Bank loan of Rs 70 crore is at in-principle approval stage, with final sanction expected the following week.

financial_highlights.change: Margin improved vs Q4 FY26 per management; no exact YoY figure stated
Spent so far: ~Rs 58 crore govt subsidy plus ~Rs 70 crore company contribution; Rs 8-10 crore non-capex spend extra

segments.name: Halol facility (silicon power semiconductors: HPD, LPD, equipment)
segments.commentary: Management sees LPD at saturation; growth to come from HPD in India and new equipment-division products. Management aims to grow top line 3-4x FY26 this year; quarterly run-rate of Rs 30+ crore targeted during FY27 excluding Odisha.

segments.name: Odisha facility (SiC epi wafers)
segments.commentary: Epitaxy phase targets epi-wafer sales from Q3 FY27; FY27 second-half epi-wafer revenue target Rs 12-15 crore. Packaging (phase 2 first step) revenue expected from Q2 FY28. Two reactors can deliver 4-, 6- and 8-inch epi; 8-inch mainly for export, 4/6-inch for domestic.

guidance_outlook: Quarterly revenue of Rs 30+ crore achievable within FY27 (excluding Odisha); Rs 50 crore per quarter expected in 6-9 months, per management, though 'it may take some more time'.
Odisha epitaxy operations to commence by end-Q2 FY27; qualification expected to take ~30 days; official inauguration targeted September 2026.
Epi-wafer revenue from Odisha from Q3 FY27; FY27 second-half epi revenue target Rs 12-15 crore.
Management targets at least 3-4x FY26 top-line growth this year, and faster bottom-line growth.
Long-term EBITDA margin aim of 15-17%, but sustainability depends on geopolitical conditions; no firm commitment given.
Epi-wafer expected yield ~85%, with a goal above 90%.
capex_capacity: Odisha power supply via 33 kV line completed; transformer charged; plant and machinery installation expected to finish end-August or mid-September 2026.
Epitaxy clean room completed; two epi reactors installed.
Phase 2 (fabrication) capex of Rs 395-400 crore still under discussion; update expected in next couple of months.
Bank term loan application of Rs 70 crore; in-principle approval received, final sanction meeting pushed a week.
Depreciation: straight-line, 15 years for plant and machinery, consistent with Halol.
demand_pricing: Price increases taken in Q1; about 80-85% of input cost increase passed on to customers, with older accepted orders lagging. New schedules carry new prices.
Further value-addition price increases seen as difficult while West Asia disruption persists.
First overseas order: 120 units of 125 mm 5 kV SCR thyristors.
Epi-wafer prospects: international customers in US and Taiwan approached; Indian government labs also interested.
Richardson Electronics: ~20,000 SiC chips supplied, under customer review; no update from customer.

qa_highlights.question: Can the core business reach Rs 50 crore quarterly revenue excluding Odisha?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes so but said it may take time; Rs 30+ crore per quarter is achievable this year, with Rs 50 crore possibly in 6-9 months after supply chain and productivity work.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Odisha project status and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Power resolved and transformer charged; epi operations to begin in about 30 days after installation; inauguration targeted September 2026. Government subsidy of Rs 58 crore received to date; company has contributed an equal amount.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Odisha phase 1 capex funding gap and bank loan size?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 130 crore spent (Rs 70 crore company plus Rs 58 crore subsidy), leaving ~Rs 100 crore; application made for Rs 70 crore bank loan.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is sustainable and what drove Q1 margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain came from price pass-through, procurement savings and redeployed staff; management aims for 15-17% but cannot confirm sustainability given geopolitical factors.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin does epi wafer carry?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected EBITDA 20-25% on epi-wafer sales; SiC devices expected to be higher margin than epi.

qa_highlights.question: What is R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 8-10% of revenue has been the long-term R&D spend norm; products in development include optically triggered thyristors (5 kV now, targeting 8 kV).

qa_highlights.question: Will RIR enter GaN?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said focus remains on SiC; sees SiC capturing power share of GaN market in about three years.

risks_watch: Bank loan final sanction (Rs 70 crore) expected next week; delay would stall phase 1 funding.
Odisha commissioning timeline: slippage from end-Q2 FY27 epi start and Q3 revenue.
Margin sustainability amid West Asia-driven input cost volatility; only 80-85% of cost increases passed through.
Phase 2 capex (Rs 395-400 crore) funding and timing not yet finalised.
Epi-wafer yield (target 85%, goal above 90%) and customer qualification in US, Taiwan and India.
Richardson Electronics SiC chip review outcome unknown.
Management declined to name products under development, citing competition; limited visibility on new product revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Odisha timelines and margins, with hedges on sustainability (margins depend on geopolitics). Evasive on long-term targets and product names, repeatedly declining forward-looking commitments. Some answers were loose or inconsistent (for example, the 3-4x growth reference and the Rs 30 crore vs Rs 50 crore run-rate), so treat guidance with caution.
key_quotes: I think this year, we will be able to easily cross about Rs. 30 plus crores per quarter.
We expect to commence epitaxy operations in the end of second quarter FY'27.
So, we expect an EBITDA somewhere in the range of 20%-25% on sale of epi wafers.
So, generally we don't give any forward -looking statements or commitments.
